stories.title: World's largest freshwater lake is recovering after decades of decline
stories.summary: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds around 20% of the world's surface freshwater, making it the most voluminous freshwater lake (Lake Superior on the United States–Canada border is the largest by surface area). This makes the lake one of the most important environments for biodiversity—in fact, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1996 because of this. Yet it has shown considerable decline over the last century, with aridification spreading across East Asia.

Mayor Rita Ali of Peoria, a city of 110,000 residents, said emergency workers had discovered a bomb at the BioUrja ethanol plant, and that a one-mile radius around that facility was evacuated on both sides of the Illinois River, which separates the two cities.

stories.title: The weird reasons why your ethernet cable might be slower than your Wi-Fi
stories.summary: It could be hardware, software or something else entirely. That's one of the primary benefits of going with a wired connection. However, that's not always true in a real world setting. Many users have noticed that ethernet cables can actually be slower than Wi-Fi. How is that even possible? In rare cases, it's simply a matter of a fast wireless connection that outpaces Ethernet speeds. stories.summary: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers. Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world. Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover. The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.
